entities.summary:
John Visconti, also known as John of Gallura, was the Judge of Gallura from 1238 to his death in 1275. He was a member of the Visconti dynasty of Pisa, which played a significant role in the politics of the Mediterranean region during the 13th century. Visconti's tenure as Judge of Gallura was marked by his efforts to consolidate power and protect the independence of his territory from rival claimants.

Visconti's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a crucial role in shaping the politics of the island of Sardinia and the surrounding region. His successors continued to build on his achievements, ensuring the Visconti dynasty remained a dominant force in the region for centuries to come.

The impact of John of Gallura's rule can still be felt today, with many historians and scholars continuing to study his life and reign as an important chapter in the history of the Mediterranean region.

The most striking aspect of Visconti's life is the sheer audacity of his ambition, as he sought to expand his territory and secure his dynasty's place in the annals of history.
